{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-x40g","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-2auf.44.11.1.1: EdhocInitiator/EdhocResponder lost struct-level ZeroizeOnDrop","description":"The `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]` was removed from both `EdhocInitiator` (line ~894) and `EdhocResponder` (line ~1257). While `SigningKey` and `StaticSecret` implement `ZeroizeOnDrop` internally, the composite `state` field (`InitiatorState`/`ResponderState`) contains derived key material (`prk_2e`, `prk_3e2m`, `prk_4e3m` — 96 bytes of HKDF-derived secrets) that will not be zeroized when the parent struct is dropped.

The inner `InitiatorState` and `ResponderState` structs retain their own `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]`, but that only triggers when the state field itself is dropped — not when the parent struct is dropped. The `poison()` methods exist on both structs but are only called on explicit error paths, not on drop.

A dropped `EdhocInitiator` after a successful handshake would leave 96 bytes of PRK material recoverable in memory.

Fix: restore `#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]` on both structs, or implement explicit `Drop` that calls `zeroize()`.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T16:49:36.74406608Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T16:49:36.74406608Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-x40g","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-2auf.44.11.1.1","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-07-24T16:49:36.88853876Z","created_by":"AI Agent","metadata":"{}"}]}
